data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Within a single evaluation, the only unambiguous evidence for a genuine reliability gain is a causal manipulation of the checklist's diagnostic validity: the panel using a randomly *shuffled* checklist (same items, destroyed construct) must show a reliability drop, whereas mere compliance may produce no drop because panelists still pattern-match to the items.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the task construct is fully captured by item-level main effects with no inter-item coherence, shuffling will not affect reliability, but the gain may still be genuine (mediated by item main effects, not order).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If panelists are trained to integrate items in a specific order, shuffling tests training fragility, not the checklist's construct validity.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Shuffled-checklist ablation: If the checklist's power lies in the *ordering* and *inter-item coherence* that define the latent construct, shuffling items destroys the construct while preserving the item pool. A genuine reliability gain should attenuate. If panelists are merely complying with items as isolated prompts (compliance), shuffling should have no effect because each item still cues the same response.
